title: Casper and the Autopsy
premise: August Voss, a night-shift taxi dispatcher in the rain-soaked city of Halvard, has a private habit: reconstructing deaths the police file as accidents. When a confession letter for a fourth death — a city coroner named Dr. Lena Marsh — arrives postmarked the day after her funeral, August realizes the letter names them as its intended recipient, and that the confessed killer is someone still inside the investigation. Following the letter's clues, August hunts for Ida Kroll, a witness officially listed as dead in the coroner's own autopsy records, discovering Marsh faked Ida's death to protect her from the man now confessing: Deputy Chief Inspector Rell. In the end, August finds Ida alive in a decommissioned morgue annex, forces Rell's confession into the open at a public inquiry, and chooses love over duty by letting Ida vanish rather than testify — keeping only the truth, not the justice, for themselves.
about_author: Quentin Iversen is the pen name of a former hospital records clerk who spent eleven years filing death certificates before turning to fiction. They write exclusively at night and claim they can still hear the fax machine.

chapters.title: The Night Frequency
chapters.summary: August Voss works the graveyard shift at Halvard Taxi, mapping the city through radio calls and noticing patterns no one else hears. A brief flashback establishes their three unofficial 'solved' deaths. POV: August. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; the reader learns August trusts patterns more than people.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: A cream envelope arrives at the dispatch office addressed to 'The one who listens.' Inside: a confession to killing Dr. Lena Marsh, postmarked the day after her funeral. August cross-checks the timeline against dispatch logs and feels the floor tilt. POV: August. Emotional beat: dread mixed with a thrill of recognition — this letter was meant for them.

chapters.title: What the Coroner Kept
chapters.summary: August visits Marsh's locked office under pretense of a cab receipt dispute and finds her private files: three of August's own cases annotated in red, plus a fourth folder labeled 'KROLL, I. — DECEASED' with an autopsy report that doesn't match its own handwriting. POV: August. Emotional beat: the hunter realizes they were being watched all along.

chapters.title: Rell at the Door
chapters.summary: Deputy Chief Inspector Rell interviews August about the letter, charming and unhurried, asking questions that reveal he already knows what's in Marsh's files. August lies smoothly for the first time in their life. POV: August. Emotional beat: attraction and suspicion braided together — Rell is dangerous in a way August can't look away from.

chapters.title: A Dead Woman's Commute
chapters.summary: August pulls taxi records: Ida Kroll rode in cab 44 eleven times in the month before her 'death,' always to the same address near the river. The driver of cab 44, an old-timer named Bo, remembers her face too well for a dead woman. POV: August. Emotional beat: hope sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Widow's Version
chapters.summary: August tracks down Marsh's estranged wife, Yrsa, who reveals Marsh had been receiving threats for months and kept a go-bag 'for the girl.' Yrsa hands over a key but begs August to stop. POV: Yrsa (first departure). Emotional beat: grief curdling into complicity — she knew and said nothing.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: Someone cuts the dispatch office phone lines during August's shift, and a cab goes missing from the lot — cab 44. August suspects Rell is closing in on the same trail. POV: August. Emotional beat: the hunt turns personal; the city itself starts feeling hostile.

chapters.title: Bo's Last Fare
chapters.summary: August finds Bo beaten and hospitalized; his last fare was a frightened young woman he drove to the old St. Alder morgue annex. Bo whispers a partial license plate before sedation. POV: August. Emotional beat: guilt — August's investigation painted a target on an innocent man.

chapters.title: The Autopsy That Lies
chapters.summary: August studies Marsh's autopsy of Ida Kroll and decodes her deliberate errors: the dental records belong to a Jane Doe, and the timestamp is impossible. Marsh didn't just hide Ida — she left a map inside the lie. POV: August. Emotional beat: awe at the dead woman's cunning; grief for an ally never met.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Devil
chapters.summary: Rell invites August to dinner, ostensibly to apologize for the interrogation. Over wine he tests them with details only the confessor could know. August realizes Rell isn't hunting the letter's author — he wrote it, as a trap for whoever Marsh trusted. POV: alternating August/Rell. Emotional beat: seduction as interrogation; August falls a little even knowing it's a blade.

chapters.title: Yrsa's Confession
chapters.summary: Yrsa admits she told Rell about the key after he threatened to expose her role in falsifying Marsh's earlier reports. She gives August the key's origin: locker 9 at St. Alder. POV: Yrsa. Emotional beat: shame and sacrifice — she chooses August's cause over her own safety.

chapters.title: Locker Nine
chapters.summary: Inside locker 9: photographs of Ida alive, dated after her autopsy, and a note in Marsh's hand — 'If you found this, the witness is where we put the ones nobody claims.' August understands: the annex cold storage. POV: August. Emotional beat: vertigo and resolve; the dead woman is speaking directly to them now.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: August is followed home by a car matching Bo's partial plate. A cat-and-mouse drive through the freight district ends with August escaping but losing the key. POV: August. Emotional beat: fear becoming fury — Rell knows how close they are.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: August's sister Maren confronts them: the obsession is costing their job, their sleep, their safety. August admits they can't stop — not for justice, but because finding Ida feels like answering Marsh across the grave. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: love as friction; family watching someone walk toward fire.

chapters.title: The Annex
chapters.summary: August breaks into the decommissioned St. Alder morgue annex at 3 a.m. and finds signs of recent habitation — then a figure with a scalpel. It's Ida Kroll, alive, feral, and convinced August is Rell's people. POV: August. Emotional beat: terror flipping to tenderness in a single held breath.

chapters.title: Ida
chapters.summary: Ida tells her story: she witnessed Rell kill a whistleblower accountant; Marsh staged her death to save her, then became a liability herself. Ida refuses to testify — last time someone promised her safety, they died. POV: Ida. Emotional beat: survival hardened into distrust; she trusts no promise, including August's.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: August faces the choice: turn Ida over to the system that failed her, or help her disappear and let Rell walk. They begin forging documents using dispatch-office resources, lying to Maren, lying to themselves. POV: August. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal — every kindness is now a crime.

chapters.title: The Trap Reversed
chapters.summary: Rell traces the annex break-in and surrounds the building. August sends an anonymous tip to three news outlets with the accountant-murder evidence Ida preserved, forcing everything into daylight before Rell can bury it. POV: Rell. Emotional beat: the predator realizing the cage was built around him.

chapters.title: Public Inquiry
chapters.summary: At a chaotic press conference-turned-hearing, the evidence detonates. Rell, cornered, nearly escapes through the crowd — until Yrsa publicly identifies him, sacrificing her anonymity. He is taken into custody screaming that the witness is a ghost. POV: multiple, mosaic-style. Emotional beat: justice arriving loud, imperfect, and public.

chapters.title: The Testimony Refused
chapters.summary: Prosecutors need Ida's live testimony; without it, Rell may walk on the murder charge. August holds the address that could deliver her — and burns it instead, giving investigators only the corroborating paper trail. POV: August. Emotional beat: the cost chosen knowingly; duty broken on purpose.

chapters.title: Where Nobody Claims Them
chapters.summary: August drives Ida north in cab 44, past the city limits, to a place where records end. At the depot, Ida almost says something more than thank you; August lets her keep it unsaid. POV: August. Emotional beat: bittersweet release — saving someone means losing them.

chapters.title: The One Who Listens
chapters.summary: Weeks later, August returns to the night shift. A new envelope arrives — blank except for a pressed flower and a postmark from the north. August smiles, files it beside Marsh's red-annotated cases, and picks up the radio. POV: August. Emotional beat: quiet peace; the listener finally heard.
